hypotheses.text: Severe structural craniofacial disruptions, specifically cleft palate and severe facial hypoplasia, occur disproportionately in fetal presentations of BRD4-related cohesinopathy compared to surviving pediatric and adult patients, where craniofacial manifestations are restricted to non-cleft cohesinopathy facial dysmorphisms.
hypotheses.rationale: In the international cohort assembled by Jouret et al. (2022), prenatal fetopathological examinations were integrated alongside postnatal pediatric and adult presentations (14 individuals total: 2 fetuses and 12 postnatal). In parallel functional animal models of BRD4 loss-of-function (Musa et al. 2024), neural crest cell deficiency of BRD4 produces severe perinatal-lethal structural facial defects including cleft palate and mid-facial clefting, indicating that fetal-stage BRD4 presentations capture a structurally disruptive lethal extreme of the CdLS6 phenotypic continuum.

evidence.text: Jouret et al. 2022 collected an international cohort of 14 new individuals with BRD4-related disorder, specifically segregating 2 fetuses undergoing fetopathological examination from 12 postnatal pediatric and adult individuals to delineate age-dependent dysmorphic features.

source.quote: We formed an international collaborative study, and collected 14 new patients, including two fetuses. We performed phenotype and genotype analysis, integrated prenatal findings from fetopathological examinations, phenotypes of pediatric patients and adults.

evidence.text: Targeted neural crest mutation of Brd4 leads to severe perinatal-lethal mid-facial clefting, cleft palate, and facial hypoplasia through failure of RUNX2 enhancer activation during osteoblast differentiation, modelling the prenatal craniofacial developmental disruption.

source.quote: Mice with BRD4 NCC loss of function died at birth with severe facial hypoplasia, cleft palate, mid-facial clefting and exencephaly.

hypotheses.text: The facial dysmorphism of CdLS6 undergoes age-dependent progressive coarsening from childhood to adulthood, transitioning from classical mild CdLS signs (such as thin vermilion of the upper lip and arched eyebrows) in pediatric cases to a distinct, recognizable non-classic cohesinopathy facial gestalt in adults.
hypotheses.rationale: Jouret et al. 2022 established that BRD4-related syndrome exhibits a recognizable facial pattern distinguishable from other cohesinopathies across age groups, while Lonardo et al. 2025 reviewed how BRD4 haploinsufficiency cases present as non-classic or atypical CdLS, a divergence that becomes most clinically apparent as facial features coarsen and mature between childhood and adult life.

evidence.text: Jouret et al. 2022 delineated the clinical spectrum across ages in 14 individuals, identifying that BRD4-related disorder confers a recognizable facial pattern across developmental stages that distinguishes it from classical cohesinopathies like NIPBL-CdLS.

source.title: Understanding the new BRD4‐related syndrome: Clinical and genomic delineation with an international cohort study
source.quote: We report the first cohort of patients with BRD4-related disorder and delineate the dysmorphic features at different ages. This work extends the phenotypic spectrum of cohesinopathies and characterize a new clinically relevant and recognizable pattern, distinguishable from the other cohesinopathies.

evidence.text: Lonardo et al. 2025 noted that BRD4 gene alterations typically produce non-classic or atypical CdLS presentations characterized by broad clinical variability and milder classic dysmorphisms.

source.title: Non-Classic Cornelia de Lange Syndrome Due to BRD4 Gene Alterations: A Literature Review
source.quote: Pathogenic variations in the NIPBL gene account for the majority of cases, but variations in several other genes, including BRD4, have been identified as causative factors for non-classic or milder forms of the syndrome.

hypotheses.text: Postnatal survival in BRD4-related syndrome is strictly conditioned on the absence of major central nervous system tube defects or severe structural osteogenic cranial base hypoplasia, which are restricted to fetal demise or termination cases.
hypotheses.rationale: Neurodevelopmental and syndromic cohorts identify BRD4 variants in surviving individuals who display neurodevelopmental delay and intellectual disability (Smal et al. 2024, Jouret et al. 2022), whereas experimental ablation of BRD4 in developing cranial and neural crest lineages results in exencephaly and early lethality (Musa et al. 2024), demonstrating that gross structural brain malformations identify non-viable fetal CdLS6 presentations.

evidence.text: Re-analysis of large neurodevelopmental disorder cohorts (745 individuals) prioritizing ultra-rare de novo candidate genes identifies surviving pediatric patients with non-lethal neurodevelopmental delay and intellectual disability rather than major cranial neural tube defects.

new_directions.question_text: What exact frequencies (numerators and denominators) of internal visceral malformations (cardiac, diaphragmatic, and renal) are documented in the 2 fetal autopsies compared to the 12 postnatal individuals in Jouret et al. 2022?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether visceral organ malformations are restricted to prenatally terminated/fetal cases will establish whether internal malformations are genuine discriminatory criteria or rare anomalies in surviving CdLS6 patients.

new_directions.question_text: Can automated deep-gestalt facial analysis algorithms (such as GestaltMatcher or Face2Gene) quantitatively separate pediatric vs adult BRD4-CdLS faces from age-matched classical NIPBL-CdLS cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Since Jouret et al. 2022 and Lonardo et al. 2025 characterize CdLS6 as having a distinct, non-classic cohesinopathy facial pattern that evolves with age, objective image analysis could confirm whether facial phenotype alone can resolve CdLS6 from classical CdLS across different age tiers.
